items.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: When Hank Jones was on the piano I mean there’s nobody can be any finer than him playing the piano

ctx.x: Yeah. And the thing is is that Bucky’s on the date, Bucky becomes number two ninety- nine percent of the time. I don’t care who’s on the piano. When Hank Jones was on the piano I mean there’s nobody can be any finer than him playing the piano and playing chords or playing rhythm or playing melody. But when Bucky and the two of them together I automatically lock in to Bucky with the bass player. And sometimes I ignored

the bass player if he wasn’t strong enough because Bucky could carry it. But we always had good strong bass players around. So I mean I really learned about the music itself, of the feel. Yes I was never super, super technical. But when I had to be you talk music. You talk music and you talk shop, whatever it is, I could be on both sides of the fence. That’s when I started to learn about what it meant to be a producer. A producer listens. You don’t go in and say okay this is it, this is what we’re going to do and…
